articleBlocks: At first, Barrel and Spring pointed in a few different directions, so the board still felt wider than one exact category.

One tempting read was "a broader umbrella topic". Barrel, Spring can point toward several nearby themes before one clue makes the exact category level visible. Barrel is the clue that narrows the board into one category with clearer boundaries.

Another nearby read was "a one-clue surface theme". Early clues often tempt you to overfit the board around one obvious surface similarity. The final answer works because it keeps every clue at the same level of specificity, not because one clue happens to fit first.
Once I read the set through a category board focused on parts, examples like "Barrel" and "Spring" stopped feeling loose and started landing cleanly.
Tip, Cap, Ink chamber keep the clues at the same category level, which is what makes the board feel like one exact set instead of a broad umbrella theme.

The answer was "Parts of a pen".
